column1: # THE VOLATILITY STATE's ROWS (2026-10-20): where an index's return sits by the volatility state, five
# rows read as one family on one day series, the way `vol_state_of` / `volStateOf` reads a path.
# `RecordBandSuite` / `record_band_tests` re-derive the shipped literals from this file.
# downside vol excess %          100 x (sqrt(sum r^2 over r < 0 / sum r^2 over r > 0) - 1) on the daily
#                                log returns: how much more the downside disperses than the upside
# vol-timing edge pts/yr         the consumer's volatility-timing rule (hold the index below the series'
#                                own 60th percentile of its 24-session realized vol, cash at 0 at or above
#                                the 80th, keep the position between), its log growth less buy-and-hold's
# vol-exit timing pts/yr         the simple volatility exit of `volexit-2026-10-20.tsv`: on the sample sd of
#                                the last 24 daily simple returns of the printed close, hold the index below
#                                1.5%, cash at the DFF rate at or above 2.0%, keep the position between;
#                                decided at a close, filled at the next, its log growth less buy-and-hold's
# vol-exit 3x interaction pts/yr the same rule on a 3x leg reset daily (2 x (the rate + 0.60%) financing over
#                                the calendar days, a 0.86% expense ratio) less the leg held, less the
#                                timing row
# high-vol fifth return pts/yr   the mean simple total return, points a year, over the sessions whose
#                                trailing 24-session sd of the printed close (known the session before) is
#                                in the span's top fifth
# Banded like `recordbands-2026-10-20.tsv`'s rows: 20000 resamples of the record, each its own length,
# built from whole 252-session blocks at uniformly drawn starts (`NumPyRng`, seed 20260918), each
# session's log return, close return, total return, rate and calendar days kept together, read at
# `RECORD_BAND_PCTS`; jointC, jointLo and jointHi a joint band over the five graded rows that a
# record-like world clears on all at once 95% of the time, their own family.  The reference rows
# carry their own joint band at the same level.
# nasdaq  THE LONG TECH RECORD, graded: Ken French's daily HiTec industry (10_Industry_Portfolios_Daily,
#         value-weighted, the 202608 CRSP database), its total return as both the signal and the
#         earnings, through 1999-03-10; then QQQ (Yahoo Finance, frozen): the printed close for the
#         signal and the adjusted close for the earnings, 1999-03-11..2026-08-20.  The session at -from
#         is the base, so the first return read is 1954-07-02's; 1954-07-01 is DFF's first date, which
#         the exit's cash leg reads.  The horizon is the record's 72 years.  HiTec is read LAG-FREE: its
#         daily returns through 1999-03-10 with the stale-price lag removed, an MA(2) inversion fitted
#         per calendar five-year block (`unlag_returns`; `-recorded` reads them as printed); QQQ, a
#         fund, as printed.
#         QQQ ALONE, reported and not graded (`<row> on QQQ 1999-2026`, series QQQ): the set's equity
#         window opens on the 2000-02 bust, which puts the first three rows on the other side of their
#         null from the long record and the exit pair at seven and two and a half times its readings
#         (4.11 and 23.20 against 0.55 and 8.87).  HiTec tracks QQQ on every one of QQQ's banded rows.
# sp500   not in this file: the S&P set reads the five on its equity window, CRSP 1954-2026, from
#         `recordbands-2026-10-20.tsv` and `volexit-2026-10-20.tsv`.
# Generated by `rust/src/bin/record_bands.rs -volstate` (twin: `jsrc/recordBands.sc -volstate`).  The
# -splice file is a `date,close,adj_close` CSV, one row a session; the -fred file is FRED's DFF:
#   record_bands -volstate -yahoo <french>/10_Industry_Portfolios_Daily.CSV -column HiTec
#       -splice <QQQ-closes.csv> -at 1999-03-10 -fred <DFF.csv> -from 1954-07-01 -to 2026-08-20
#       -set nasdaq -series HiTec+QQQ -refseries QQQ -joint 0.05 -header
